text:
natalie yang: hi @emma — I missed the 30-day window to add my newborn (born 2026-04-02). Is there any way to still get them onto medical/dental/vision retroactive to birth?
emma (People Ops): hi @natalie — sorry you ran into that. Standard policy is 30 days for QLE newborn additions. We can submit an exception request to the carrier if there's a documented reason for the delay. Why was the window missed?
natalie yang: I was in the hospital and then tried to submit during travel; I thought I had until the end of the month. I have the birth certificate dated 2026-04-02 and hospital discharge summary. Can we ask for retro coverage back to 4/2?
emma (People Ops): hospital stay is a common acceptable reason. Please upload the birth certificate and discharge summary to the portal and include a short note explaining the delay. We will open an exception case and request retro enrollment. Note: carriers decide exception outcomes; we advocate but cannot guarantee approval.
benefits-bot: @natalie yang Upload path: Benefits -> Manage Dependents -> Add Dependent -> "Upload Proof". Select document types: Birth Certificate, Hospital Discharge. Accepted: PDF/JPG/PNG. Max 10MB. Use filename: yang_newborn_birthcert_20260402.pdf. Toggle "Contains sensitive info" if docs include SSN.
natalie yang: Uploaded yang_birthcert_20260402.pdf and discharge_summary_20260405.pdf and added a note explaining the hospitalization and travel. Also added newborn SSN in secure form.
hr-portal-bot: Files received. Case EXC-2026-311 opened. Verification queued; benefits will submit exception to carrier. Expect 5-7 business days for carrier response.
emma (People Ops): Thanks @natalie. A few payroll notes while we wait: if carrier approves retro, payroll can process a premium adjustment retro to the effective date; that typically posts as a correction on the next payroll cycle. If carrier denies, we can discuss alternative timelines and potential OOP costs. @sam payroll can confirm timing.
sam payroll: @emma @natalie If carrier grants retro to 2026-04-02 we'll run a premium reconciliation and any refund or owed premium will show on the following paycheck as an adjustment line. If verification/exception completes after payroll cutoff dates, timing may slip one additional pay period. We won't withhold more than what the carrier approves retroactive.
natalie yang: Appreciate the clarity. If carrier denies, can we appeal?
emma (People Ops): Yes, if denied we'll request a formal denial letter from the carrier and then submit an internal appeal packet; we can escalate with supporting docs. It helps to include clinician notes or a timeline showing inability to enroll within 30 days.
benefits-bot: Tips for exception packet: 1) Birth cert + discharge + timeline note. 2) Proof of attempted submission (email/screenshot) if you have it. 3) SSN submitted via secure form. 4) Contact number for case follow-up.
natalie yang: I added a screenshot of my attempted portal session from 4/28 where the upload failed. Hope that helps.
hr-portal-bot: Exception packet updated with additional screenshot. Case EXC-2026-311 status: Submitted to carrier.
emma (People Ops): I'll monitor and let you know as soon as we hear back. If carrier asks for anything else they'll contact through this case and we'll notify you. Thanks for uploading everything promptly — fingers crossed. :crossed_fingers:
